title: Log one real state transition
prompt: Controller borrows an Audit interface. start turns a stopped controller on and logs "started" exactly once. Further start calls return false without a log. stop turns it off without logging. The Audit reference must outlive Controller.
signature: class Audit; class Controller: bool start(), void stop(), bool running() const
driver: struct Capture:Audit{int calls=0;void record(std::string_view s)override{if(s=="started")++calls;}};int main(){Capture log;Controller c(log);c.start();c.start();std::cout<<std::boolalpha<<c.running()<<" "<<log.calls<<"\n";}

tests.label: First start
tests.expression: ([]{struct C:Audit{int n=0;void record(std::string_view){++n;}} a;Controller c(a);return c.start()&&c.running()&&a.n==1;})()
tests.hint: Change state once and send one event.

tests.label: Stop and restart
tests.hint: A new transition after stop can log.

tests.label: No startup log
tests.hint: Construction does not start the controller.

hints: A reference borrows the logger; it does not create or destroy it.
explanation: Composition lets a Controller use a supplied component. Its state transition decides when to call that component, so a rejected repeat cannot create a false audit event.
